title: Hydrogen adsorption on graphene sheets and nonporous graphitized thermal carbon black at low surface coverage
material_description: GS | graphene sheets prepared from thermally expanded r-GO synthesized by a modified Hummers method; EDS (atom %): C 78.88, O 13.62, P 3.24, Cl 0.12, Nb 4.14
source_location: main.pdf p.4, Fig. 4a, series GS@77K, point 1
notes: archive: GS_77K_fig4a_m1.json; digitized pressure 0.13263157894736843 kPa converted to bar (x0.01); uptake digitized in mmol g-1 (axis n_exc/mmol g-1), wt% computed as W1 = 0.201588 x mmol/g; Sample: GS, thermally expanded r-GO (modified Hummers method, ref 16); EDS shows non-carbon elements (O, P, Cl, Nb) which the authors call impurity; no residual-catalyst role is stated, so recorded here only. Table 2: pore volume 0.2248 cm3/g entered as total pore volume, micropore volume 0.0301 cm3/g, by DFT on Ar 87 K data, BET area 220.5 m2/g (probe gas taken as Ar: the only adsorption gas named for textural analysis, Ar at 87 K, Fig. 2; BET range not stated). Degas: 363.15 K 3 h then 423.15 K 12 h (final step stored). Sample mass 0.1676 g. Gas purity: ultra-high-purity grade, no number. No free-volume determination described; paper says the mean of three measurements was used, no spread given. Reconciled (C): uptake_mmol_g, pressure_bar and digitization_uncertainty_wt_pct are the mean of the A and B digitizations of this marker (match line 20; uncertainty = max(half difference, 1% of uptake-axis span)); uptake_wt_pct = W1 = 0.201588 x mean mmol/g. Reconciliation (C): residual_metal_element set to Nb, from EDS Table 1 (GS: Nb 4.14 atom %), which the authors call an impurity of the tested GS sample (Conclusions); the paper gives no origin and no wt%, so residual_metal_wt_pct is empty.

basis_evidence: As per Gibbs's definition of the adsorption, the excess adsorption amount nexc can be correlated with absolute adsorption amount nabs as nexc = nabs - va*rho_b (Eq. 1); Fig. 4: 'Isotherms of excess amount of hydrogen'
